user_stories.title: Implement AgentTuple dataclass with 4 fields
acceptance_criteria: AgentTuple is a Pydantic dataclass with instruction (str), context (str), tools (list), and model (ModelConfig) fields
instruction field is required and must not be empty after stripping whitespace
context field defaults to empty string
tools field defaults to empty list
model field is required and must be a ModelConfig instance
AgentTuple.build_prompt() method returns instruction with optional context appended
AgentTuple can be serialized to/from JSON using Pydantic methods
Pydantic validation raises clear errors for invalid configurations
Unit tests cover all validation rules and edge cases
Type hints are present for all fields and methods
user_stories.notes: This is the core 4-tuple abstraction Î¦ = (Instruction, Context, Tools, Model). Foundation for all other components. Must use Pydantic v2 dataclass for validation and serialization.

user_stories.title: Implement Observation result structure
acceptance_criteria: Observation is a Pydantic BaseModel with result_summary (str), artifacts (dict), and error_logs (list) fields
result_summary field is required and describes the execution outcome
artifacts field defaults to empty dict and holds structured outputs
error_logs field defaults to empty list and captures errors/warnings
Observation.add_error() method appends messages to error_logs
Observation.add_artifact() method adds key-value pairs to artifacts
Observation can be serialized to/from JSON for state persistence
Unit tests verify all methods and serialization behavior
Observation supports extensible metadata for future enhancements
user_stories.notes: Required by item 002 for state history tracking. Must be serializable for persistence between orchestration steps.

user_stories.title: Implement ModelConfig for LLM backend
acceptance_criteria: ModelConfig is a Pydantic dataclass with name, api_base, api_key, temperature, and max_tokens fields
name field is required (e.g., 'glm-4.7', 'glm-4-flash')
api_base field is required and must start with http:// or https://
api_key field defaults to empty string
temperature field defaults to 0.7 and must be between 0.0 and 2.0
max_tokens field defaults to 2048 and must be greater than 0
ModelConfig.to_openai_kwargs() returns dict compatible with OpenAI client initialization
Pydantic validation ensures api_base is valid URL format
Unit tests cover all validation rules and edge cases
ModelConfig is simple enough to be wrapped by ModelRegistry in item 004
user_stories.notes: Designed to work with Z.ai GLM models via OpenAI-compatible API. Must be extensible for item 004's ModelRegistry with tiers.

user_stories.title: Define Tool protocol interface
acceptance_criteria: Tool is a typing.Protocol with name (str), description (str), and async execute(**kwargs) method
Protocol uses @runtime_checkable decorator for isinstance() validation
validate_tool() function checks if object implements Tool protocol
validate_tool() raises TypeError with clear message if object is not a valid tool
Tool protocol is flexible (duck typing) - any object with matching signature qualifies
Mock tools (EchoTool, CalculatorTool, ErrorTool) demonstrate the interface
Unit tests verify protocol validation catches invalid tools
Tool interface accommodates item 003's requirement for 'name, description, execute' pattern
Tool protocol documentation explains how to create custom tools
user_stories.notes: Uses Protocol (not base class) for maximum flexibility. Must work with item 003's ToolRegistry and diverse tool implementations.

user_stories.title: Implement mock tools for testing
acceptance_criteria: EchoTool has name='echo', description, and async execute(message) that returns echoed message
CalculatorTool has name='calculator', description, and async execute(operation, a, b) that performs arithmetic
CalculatorTool supports add, subtract, multiply, divide operations
CalculatorTool raises ValueError for division by zero and unknown operations
ErrorTool has name='error_tool' and async execute() that always raises RuntimeError
All mock tools implement Tool protocol and pass validate_tool() check
Unit tests verify each mock tool executes correctly in async context
ErrorTool tests verify errors are properly raised
user_stories.notes: Mock tools enable testing SubAgent without real LLM calls. Item 003 will replace these with real tools (calculator, code_execute, web_search_mock, file_read).

user_stories.title: Implement SubAgent base class with async execute()
acceptance_criteria: SubAgent is initialized with an AgentTuple
SubAgent has async execute() method that returns an Observation
execute() builds prompt from tuple.instruction and tuple.context using build_prompt()
execute() creates AsyncOpenAI client from tuple.model configuration
execute() calls LLM with prompt and available tools
execute() processes tool_calls if present in LLM response
execute() invokes tools using async execute(**kwargs) method
execute() captures tool execution results in artifacts
execute() captures all errors in error_logs and returns partial results
execute() never propagates exceptions - always returns Observation
SubAgent only accesses its assigned context and tools (isolation guarantee)
_prepare_tools() converts tool objects to OpenAI function-calling format
_find_tool(name) locates tool by name in tuple.tools
Unit tests use mocked OpenAI client to verify execution flow
Tests verify tool invocation, error handling, and isolation
user_stories.notes: Core execution engine. Must be async for concurrent sub-agent operation. Isolation is critical - each SubAgent must only access its assigned context/tools.

user_stories.title: Implement AgentFactory for sub-agent creation
acceptance_criteria: AgentFactory has create(tuple_def) method that returns SubAgent instance
create() validates tuple_def before creating SubAgent
Validation checks instruction is not empty after stripping whitespace
Validation checks all tools implement Tool protocol using validate_tool()
Validation checks model.name and model.api_base are not empty
create() raises ValueError for invalid tuple configurations
create() raises TypeError for invalid tools with clear error messages
AgentFactory has async create_and_execute() convenience method
create_and_execute() creates agent and awaits execute() in one call
Unit tests verify validation catches all invalid configurations
Unit tests verify factory creates valid SubAgent instances
Factory is ready for integration with item 002's Orchestrator
user_stories.notes: Provides clean interface for Orchestrator (item 002) to spawn sub-agents. Validation ensures bad configurations fail early with clear errors.
